headings.text: C. Complete Keyboard Navigation & Focus Indicators
D. Screen Reader Optimization & ARIA Attributes

paragraphs.text: To fulfill this commitment, we adhere as strictly as possible to the World Wide Web Consortium’s (W3C) Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 (WCAG 2.1) at the Level AA success criteria. These guidelines explain how to make web content more usable and accessible for individuals with sensory, cognitive, and mobility impairments.
Accessibility is built directly into our design system and frontend implementation through the following core techniques:

Every page features semantic HTML5 landmarks (<header>, <main>, <nav>, <section>, <footer>), ensuring screen readers can navigate directly between major landmarks without obstruction. Only a single <h1> is rendered per page.

Color palettes meet or exceed the required minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal body text and 3:1 for large headings against their background. Typography dynamically scales up to 200% via standard browser zoom without truncation or horizontal scrolling loss.

All interactive elements—including mega menus, dropdown toggles, modal dialogues, tab filters, and quote calculation forms—are fully operable via standard keyboard (<kbd class="px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-100 border text-xs font-mono">Tab</kbd>, <kbd class="px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-100 border text-xs font-mono">Enter</kbd>, <kbd class="px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-slate-100 border text-xs font-mono">Space</kbd>, and arrow keys). Focus states feature high-visibility emerald focus rings.

Images feature descriptive alternative text (alt="...") or are explicitly marked decorative (aria-hidden="true"). Complex interactive widgets utilize appropriate WAI-ARIA states (aria-expanded, aria-controls, role="region").
Our digital assets undergo routine accessibility auditing and manual validation using representative assistive technologies, including:

While we strive for comprehensive accessibility across every digital asset, some older historical PDF archives or third-party mapping widgets may not yet fully conform to WCAG 2.1 AA standards. We are actively working to remediate these assets or provide accessible plain-text equivalents upon request.

We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Techsteps. If you encounter accessibility barriers, require documentation in alternative formats (such as large print, accessible PDF, or plain text), or need assistance booking a service, please contact our Accessibility Officer:
If you are not satisfied with how we respond to your complaint, you can contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS) at equalityadvisoryservice.com.

Cookies are small alphanumeric text files stored directly in your web browser or local device storage when you visit websites. They enable digital platforms to identify your browser, remember session states (such as active quote requests and navigation preferences), and generate aggregate performance analytics.

Under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR) and the UK GDPR, we are legally required to inform you regarding the cookies we deploy, their functional purpose, and obtain your explicit consent for any non-essential technologies.
Our digital architecture strictly minimizes tracking. We categorize cookies into three clear operational classifications:

Essential cookies are technically required for core website functionality, security, network routing, and accessibility. They allow you to navigate pages securely, submit interactive quote request forms, verify anti-CSRF tokens, and save your legal consent choices. You cannot disable these cookies in our settings without impairing website security.

These cookies enable our website to remember choices you make (such as your chosen division or preferred quote contact method) and provide enhanced, personalized navigational efficiency across visits.

We use privacy-respecting aggregated analytics to assess website traffic patterns, popular service pages, and system load times. All telemetry is aggregated and anonymized; we do not build cross-site behavioural profiles, monetize browsing data, or sell data to third-party advertising brokers.
You maintain full autonomy over the storage of cookies on your device:
We review our cookie inventory annually or upon deploying new digital client services. Any updates will be published on this page with an updated revision date.
